transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-15 10:30 PST — Duration 46m — Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Priya (Strata Eng Mgr), Ethan (Strata SRE), Marta (Strata CTO)

Auto-summary: quick throughput check-in focused on cont. batching and queue shaping. Reviewed overnight replay results (mixed), identified three hot routes with tail spikes, agreed to run a longer adaptive-window replay and share p99/p95 by route. Action items assigned for traces and pricing update.

Topics: continuous batching behavior, concurrency targets, queue depth shaping, cache warming, fallback strategies.

00:00 Jordan: okay, uh, good morning everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call?
00:06 Priya: Priya here, morning.
00:08 Ethan: Ethan.
00:10 Marta: Marta on.
00:12 Jordan: Jordan (Redwood) and Maya (Redwood) — quick agenda, we looked at overnight runs, saw a couple of p99 spikes, want to tune the adaptive window and warm-pool sizing, and talk next steps.
00:30 Maya: I pulled the replay results into a quick sheet — link shared in chat — it's the run with continuous batching enabled, base concurrency 48, burst policy on. The thing we noticed is the long-tail on three routes A, B, and C, route C is the small prompt but high QPS.
00:48 Priya: yeah route C is the webhook sync endpoint — small prompts but lots of concurrent short-lived requests, so batching helps but the queuing latency sometimes dominates.
:01:05 Ethan: just to call out, our arrival pattern is very spiky at 11am local — short bursts of 30s at 250rps, then back down, so average stats hide the peaks.
01:22 Maya: exact, the continuous batcher groups tokens inside a 60ms adaptive window in this run; that reduces token cost but if concurrency is topped out you see queue growth. We saw queue depth hit 72 in the 11:02 spike, and p99 shot to 1.8s.
01:48 Jordan: are those 1.8s requests mostly waiting for a new generation or is it tail GPU latency?
01:54 Maya: mostly waiting — KV cache warm is okay, GPU p50/p95 is stable. It's the queuing headroom that's the limiter. We simulated raising concurrency from 48 to 64 and it reduced p99 to ~700ms but increased cost ~14%.
02:12 Marta: okay that tradeoff is important for us — we have SLA target 500ms p95 for interactive flows, and 2s for async.
02:20 Priya: can we do a mixed policy: raise concurrency during the 30s bursts and then drop back?
02:28 Maya: yes, Redwood supports burst capacity and autoscale policies; we can set a fast ramp to allow +50% concurrency for windows under 60s. The catch is whether the model cold start (KV reload) penalizes short bursts.
02:42 Ethan: cold start was minimal in our tests, not the blocker. Another thought is queue shaping — use a leaky-bucket so requests exceed Xms are dropped to fallback smaller model or return 503 gracefully.
03:00 Jordan: good point — we can pair an A/B fallback rule: when queue depth > 60 route-level, route C falls back to smaller 7B quantized model with 30% lower token cost and slightly higher hallucination risk.
03:18 Priya: we need to quantify the quality delta though, product cares.
03:22 Maya: agreed — we can run side-by-side quality checks with the same prompt set, and Redwood Optimize will surface the confusion metrics. We'll prepare an eval for the three routes.
03:40 Marta: also, how does continuous batching interact with prefix caching for our authenticated flows? We use per-user prefixes.
03:48 Maya: per-user prefix reduces cache hit ratio; we saw hit rate drop to ~38% on route B. The recommendation was to shard prefixes or use a short shared system prompt plus user-specific tokens to help increase hits.
04:07 Ethan: hmm, we can rework prompt engineering to move stable context into the shared prompt — that's on us to test.
04:15 Jordan: quick aside for compliance — Marta, you raised SSO/KMS last week — any blockers?
04:21 Marta: mostly fine, SOC2 docs were ok, but we need a session with your security engineering to confirm HSM integration for private deployment.
04:30 Jordan: we'll set that up; Maya can join to explain the private control plane handshake.
04:36 Maya: yes I can; also note that the VPC peering setup changed how we route logs, so audit log retention might need a config.
04:45 Priya: ok — back to throughput, what's the plan for the adaptive windows?
04:50 Maya: I'd like to run three replays: 20ms, 60ms (current), and 120ms windows. That shows the cost/latency frontier. We also want a 12-hour replay to capture cross-hour bursts, not just 1-hour.
05:06 Ethan: we can provide a 48-hour trace for better fidelity.
05:09 Maya: perfect — for the replay we'll include per-token cost estimates and p50/p95/p99 by route and by time-slice.
05:18 Jordan: what about warm pool sizing for the model instances? We noticed warm pool idle time was 2.2s in the run.
05:25 Maya: we suggest a small warm pool floor matched to your 99th percentile concurrent active users. For route C (short chats) set min instances to cover baseline 120rps to keep cold starts rare. We'll suggest specific numbers after we analyze the 48h trace.
05:42 Priya: can you share the replay sheet and the raw CSVs you used?
05:46 Maya: sheet is shared — link is tinyurl.com/redwood-strata-replay (in chat). Raw CSV is uploaded to the S3 bucket we agreed on; I'll DM credentials to Ethan.
05:58 Ethan: got it. One more operational question — metrics ingestion frequency, will Redwood emit per-request traces to our tracing backends?
06:06 Maya: yes we can push spans to your Jaeger/Lightstep with trace IDs; there's an option to sample 100% for pilot.
06:15 Jordan: okay recap and next steps — Maya will run adaptive-window replays (20/60/120ms) over a 12h and 24h window, include p50/p95/p99 and cost CSVs; Ethan to upload 48h trace; Jordan to send updated pilot pricing. We'll also schedule security deep-dive.
06:37 Marta: that works, one ask — include model fallback quality evals for route C so product can approve.
06:44 Maya: noted, we'll run the eval harness and attach confusion/ROUGE-like scores as a short report.
06:52 Priya: thanks everyone.
06:54 Jordan: thanks all — we'll sync next Tuesday same time unless we need an earlier quick follow.
07:00 (meeting end)

Notes on transcription: small mis-hears around specific numbers (e.g., concurrency sometimes transcribed as 48/64), some vendor names may be slightly off.
